messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) the melting/freezing point of pure water drops to roughly **–2 °C**.  
This is because the phase boundary between ice and liquid water shifts to lower temperatures as the external pressure is reduced; at 10 kPa the equilibrium temperature is about 2 °C below the standard 0 °C at 1 atm.
